bullets.title: NVDA: Vera Rubin delivers 10x throughput vs Blackwell; bullish vibe shift into earnings
bullets.body: MS TMT desk flags NVDA manufacturing partners producing ~1,000 racks/day (>$600B quarterly revenue potential, chip-limited), while Vera Rubin NVL72 hits 800k tokens/s vs GB200's 80k at identical 150MW draw. Jensen Huang publicly backed free/open-source Chinese AI models (Kimi K3) as compute demand drivers, not threats — echoing the DeepSeek playbook. Stock fell pre-market on broad semi weakness despite the bullish fundamental narrative.

bullets.title: AMD: Anthropic 2GW MI450 partnership + $5B equity investment; Wolfe/KeyBanc both Overweight
bullets.body: AMD and Anthropic formalized a deal to deploy up to 2GW of MI450 Instinct GPUs in Helios rack systems, with 1GW starting 1H27; AMD commits $5B strategic equity in Anthropic. Wolfe sees $30-40B incremental CY27-28 revenue, each GW implying $15-20B revenue and $3-4 EPS; maintains $650 PT (stock ~$544). KeyBanc maintains OW with $725 PT (41x 2027E EPS of $17.84), calling AMD a credible AI accelerator challenger to NVDA at 30x 2027E vs peers at 47x.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Bears getting louder on Gemini 3.5 Pro delay; earnings tonight are the key test
bullets.body: GOOGL delayed Gemini 3.5 Pro (still testing) while beginning Gemini 4 pre-training — bears cite this as evidence of coding/agentic AI weakness and talent loss. Citi calls for YT +11%+, Search +17-18%, GCP ~75%; key reads are GCP growth vs +64.5% consensus and clarity on 2027 capex ($300-350B range). Reddit reportedly considering shutting off Google's AI training content access, which Citi flags as disintermediation risk to ad business.

bullets.title: META: Jefferies sizes $14-18B hardware opportunity from AI glasses + ams OSRAM microLED partnership
bullets.body: Jefferies hosted a webcast sizing META's AI smart glasses hardware opportunity at $14-18B, with ams OSRAM contributing €75/unit across 11 technologies including 4K microLED display. Separately, META is developing an internal AI router called 'Switchboard' to route inference tasks to cheaper smaller models, with potential enterprise productization. MS TMT also flagged META as the best-positioned ad-based internet name with Anthropic compute deal optionality adding ~$25/share upside.

bullets.title: GEV: EPS miss on accounting but orders/FCF blow out; stock -10% as cycle-durability fears dominate
bullets.body: GEV Q2 EPS $2.47 missed $3.10 consensus but revenue $11.1B beat $10.8B; FY FCF guidance nearly doubled to $11.5-12.5B from $6.5-7.5B and FY revenue raised to $45.5-46.5B. Added 20GW new gas contracts (vs buyside 15-18GW expectation), lifting equipment under contract target to 125GW, and announced a 30GW capacity target for 2030. MS post-call note says the stock appeared crowded pre-earnings; only 2GW of the 20GW adds are firm orders (rest are slot reservation agreements), raising cycle-durability concerns.

bullets.title: T: Strong Q2 beat — 432K postpaid phone adds, raised $10B buyback; stock +3-4%
bullets.body: AT&T Q2 EPS $0.65 beat $0.59 consensus; wireless postpaid phone net adds 432K vs 325K estimate; fiber net adds 367K; EBITDA $12.38B vs $12.1B estimate. Company raised share repurchases to $10B for 2026 and maintained FY FCF guidance of $18B+. Lumen integration progressing; net leverage rises to ~3.2x post-EchoStar, targeting return to 2.5x within 3 years.

bullets.title: SMCI: +12-16% on $60B Q4 bookings; Vera Rubin rack demand drives potential 50% FY27 revenue growth
bullets.body: SMCI preannounced $60B+ new orders in Q4 for next-gen AI (Vera Rubin) rack systems — enough to drive FY27 revenue up ~50% y/y excluding new 12-month orders — while targeting 16% gross margins vs consensus 8%. MS TMT identifies SPCX as a customer. DELL +2.4% and HPE +1.9% traded in sympathy pre-market.

bullets.title: NOW: Proxy for AI software winner/loser debate — cRPO and forward guide the critical read
bullets.body: UBS models NOW demand trends stable, forecasting 100bps cRPO beat (20.0% vs 19.8% guided). MS TMT desk flags NOW as the key test of whether cloud software wins or loses to AI disruption, requiring a clean beat on cRPO (+21% vs 19.5% guide) and strong forward guidance to reverse bearish narrative. Stock struggling with the winner/loser AI debate heading into print.

bullets.title: TXN: Street expects beat-and-raise; consensus models +11.4% seq revenue to $5.38B, 3Q guide >$5.7B
bullets.body: JPM survey respondents model TXN Q2 revenue of $5.38B (+11.4% seq) with a 3Q guide above $5.7B (+7%+ seq) needed for sentiment; gross margin guide of 61%+ also cited as critical. Over 75% of respondents expect further TXN price hikes in 2H. Hedge fund longs are at multi-year crowded levels (score 8/10) with a 9.5% implied move.

bullets.title: AAPL: TSMC foundry price hikes to add $20+ to iPhone BOM; MacBook/iMac AI redesign confirmed
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags TSMC raising advanced-node prices 5-10% in 2027 (HPC customers pay additional 10-15% premium), with Apple fully dependent on TSMC for 2nm-class chips — implying at least $20 iPhone BOM impact. Separately, Bloomberg/StreetAccount confirm Apple is redesigning MacBook and iMac lineups for fall 2026 and 2027 to meet AI-capable machine demand.

bullets.title: SHOP: Added to JPMorgan Analyst Focus List; stock down 2.6% in Canada pre-market
bullets.body: Shopify was added to the JPMorgan Analyst Focus List in the morning session, but the stock traded lower by 2.6% to C$169.15 in Canadian trading. No revised price target or rating change was included in the alert.

bullets.title: ARM: Wells Fargo cuts PT to $350 from $410
bullets.body: Wells Fargo reduced its ARM Holdings price target to $350 from $410, with no rating change disclosed in the alert. The cut represents a 15% reduction in target, signaling reduced upside estimates likely tied to broader semiconductor softness.

bullets.title: LITE: Barclays upgrades to Overweight; photonics sector flagged as durable higher-beta semi play
bullets.body: Barclays upgraded LITE to Overweight in the ESG/sector roundup. A separate social post flags LITE, AAOI, COHR, and NOK as durable photonics names with higher beta to the semiconductor sector. JPM earnings preview shows LITE reports 8/11 after close with F4Q26 guide of $960M-$1.01B revenue and 35-36% operating margin.

bullets.title: ANET/CIEN/CLS/CSCO: JPM bullish on DC capex durability; North America DC capacity hit record 75GW in Q2
bullets.body: JPM's Joe Cardoso argues fears about data center capex durability are overblown, citing North America DC capacity reaching a record 75GW in Q2 (+13GW QoQ) with planned capacity at 210GW vs 116GW one year ago. JPM buyside survey covers ANET (reports 8/4, F2Q guide $2.8B rev), CLS (reports 7/27, F2Q guide $4.15-4.45B), CSCO (reports 8/13, F4Q guide $16.7-16.9B), and CIEN.

bullets.title: DKNG: Stifel cuts estimates ahead of Q2 earnings on unfavorable NBA/World Cup outcomes
bullets.body: Stifel reduced OSB/iCasino estimates across the sector citing unfavorable sports results and expects Q2 misses for DKNG (and FLUT, SRAD). FLUT highlighted as favorable near-term risk/reward on iCasino momentum and improving parlay mix despite the headwinds. Sector promotional intensity is easing and Stifel maintains constructive medium-term view.

bullets.title: IONQ: Jefferies Buy, $85 PT; quantum sector in focus on Trump executive orders and Quantinuum IPO
bullets.body: Jefferies reiterates IonQ Buy with $85 PT amid Trump's ~$2B federal quantum program backing strategic stakes in nine companies. Quantinuum's Nasdaq IPO was 20x+ oversubscribed, priced above range and trading ~30% above IPO price. D-Wave is also rated Buy at $45; Rigetti Hold at $20.

bullets.title: EFX: JPM maintains OW but cuts PT to $210 from $230; Government vertical -4% y/y stings
bullets.body: Equifax Q2 adjusted EPS $2.25 beat $2.21 estimate, and organic constant-currency revenue grew +9.5% y/y, but the stock dropped 3.9% post-earnings on Government vertical weakness (-4% y/y vs mid-double-digit growth in Q1). FY26 o/cc revenue guidance midpoint raised to +10.3%; 3Q guide +8.3-10.3% with adjusted EPS $2.15-2.25. JPM JPM sees Government revenue returning to growth in H2 but lacks specifics.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler ROIC debate intensifies: $1.4T capex, 4x compute expansion targeted through 2028
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley examines how GOOGL, AMZN, and META will prove ROIC on $1.4T+ combined hyperscaler capex, with capacity buildout projected to reach $2T by 2027. OpenAI separately raised its compute spending projection to $750B through 2030 (from $600B) and is contracting 3.2GW of Georgia Power capacity for 2028-2032. Databricks CEO reports GPU exhaustion across multiple regions, driving fundraising.

bullets.title: UBER: Analyst argues TSLA's pivot to 1-2 passenger niche is minuscule (<1% of auto sales); UBER wins at scale
bullets.body: One analyst argues Tesla is evolving toward the 1-2 passenger market which represents less than 1% of auto sales, while UBER is already at scale for that use case and will benefit additively from 10-15 driverless partners building on its platform.

bullets.title: DOCN: GPU list prices raised ~30% avg effective 08/01; H100 reserved +20%, on-demand +65%
bullets.body: Citi TMT desk notes DigitalOcean raised GPU list prices roughly 30% on average effective August 1 (H100 Reserved +20%, On-Demand +65% vs spot). Citi views this as supporting unit economics of the buildout and broadly positive for GPU cloud pricing power.
